text:
Maya: quick RFC follow-up — decision point: where do we store quantization/precision profiles long-term? model artifact (in model.tar) vs serving config overlay? need a single contract before the runtime refactor.

Jon: leaning toward model artifact. profiles are model-specific (per-arch/weights) and should travel with the model. simpler offline reproducibility + CI.

Sara: +1 for model shipping, but we need overlays in the serving layer for per-route overrides, canaries, and emergency rollbacks. can't force every customer to rebuild model tar to tweak a fallback.

Lukas: can we have both? canonical profile in model artifact + a thin overlay in the control plane that references the artifact and applies diffs. key is a versioned compatibility fingerprint so runtime can quickly validate.

Maya: that matches my mental model. proposal sketch:
```json
{
  "profile_version": "v1",
  "model_fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "precision_defaults": {"weights": "int8", "activations": "fp8"},
  "fallback_chain": ["int8", "fp16"],
  "quality_guard": 0.98,
  "telemetry_keys": ["per_token_bleu", "degradation_score"]
}
```

Jon: that schema looks good. couple questions: 1) who generates the fingerprint? 2) where do we store the delta overlays? and 3) should the runtime refuse to apply overlays if fingerprint mismatch?

Sara: answers: 1) the model build pipeline (modelpack) should emit the fingerprint and profile. 2) overlays live in the control plane / per-customer config (encrypted), and we snapshot them in audit logs. 3) yes, runtime should require a compatible fingerprint unless operator explicitly allows mismatch with a risk flag. safer.

Lukas: ops note — we should design the runtime check to be cheap: metadata header in the model blob with a small compatibility vector and a monotonic profile_version. no heavy I/O on request path; validate at load time.

Jon: telemetry + regression detection: want an automated health check that runs the profile's eval set in the canary, and blocks rollout if quality_guard fails. can we wire that to Console?

Maya: yep. action: profile includes an embedded eval-set reference id (not raw data) so Console can fetch and run lightweight regression tests. canary pipeline will reject if measured < quality_guard.

Sara: also we need a compact on-disk encoding for profiles so model tar doesn't bloat. suggest delta-encoding + protobuf + zstd. runtime can parse in <5ms.

Lukas: +1. also recommend we include a "safety_net" field: an ordered list of precision variants to attempt when selected precision fails runtime assertions (OOM, NaN, perf regressions). example: ["fp8","int8","fp16"].

Maya: propose we adopt this implementation plan:
1) modelpack emits profile v1 + fingerprint (start of next sprint)
2) control plane accepts overlays and stores audit trail (next sprint)
3) runtime load-time validation + safety_net fallback (sprint after)
4) Console canary / eval gate integration (follow-up)

Jon: sounds good. can we add a short migration playbook for older models with no profile? fallback to conservative defaults (weights:int8 activations:fp16) and require a canary run before permissive routing.

Sara: I'll draft the playbook and a tiny CLI to generate profile patches.

quant-bot: new artifact uploaded: model-abc v2 (fingerprint sha256:deadbeef). profile missing — flagged for migration. :warning:

Maya: thanks @Sara — assign the playbook to you. @Jon please add the runtime check item to infra board. @Lukas please draft the compact encoding PR. I'll open a short RFC addendum with the schema above.

Jon: will do.

Sara: starting on playbook now, will ping for review.

Lukas: prepping encoding PR. will include microbench numbers (<2ms parse on p4-node).

Maya: end-state: model artifact + optional overlays, versioned fingerprints, runtime load-time validation, safety_net fallback, canary eval gate. everyone ok? :thumbsup:

Jon: :+1:

Sara: :thumbsup:

Lukas: :+1:

quant-bot: ticket created: ML-3125 "profile storage & runtime contract" assigned to Maya, Sara, Jon, Lukas.
